lab: EIGRP Equal and Unequal Cost Load Balancing
topology: Classic IOS EIGRP AS100 diamond R1–R2/R3–R4, PC1 behind R1 and SRV1 behind R4. Eight prepared server IP bindings .40.10–17 create separate default CEF source/destination flows. Practice begins with equal metrics but maximum-paths 1. Final R1 paths have metrics10240/20480, RD7680, maximum-paths2, variance2 and balanced traffic-share counts2/1.
implemented: Fifteenth ENARSI Layer3 Technologies lab with independent practice/completed documents, six-row addressing plan, staged instructions, validated reference/verification commands and current-origin/path/query permalinks. Existing UI, terminal, artwork and layout are preserved.

Corrected EIGRP forwarding shares: balanced installation assigns integer traffic-share counts using the highest installed metric divided by each path metric, rounded down. Detailed show ip route and CEF now consume the same weights. Equal paths use1/1; the prepared unequal paths use2/1. Maximum-paths remains an installation cap and strict RD < retained FD still excludes nonfeasible alternatives.

Corrected traffic-share min across-interfaces: all variance-eligible paths remain in the operational RIB, with zero forwarding share on worse paths. CEF excludes the zero-share backup; DUAL reassigns share1 if it becomes the only successor after uplink failure. Route selection preserves zero-share EIGRP multipath backups without changing zero-share static forwarding behavior.

Initial observation requires three accepted requests and parent-linked replies for each of eight server addresses over R1/R2/R4. ECMP requires those eight actual flows to use both branches with stable per-flow egress. Unequal variance1 requires only the primary installed while the alternate remains feasible; variance2 admits both and actual weighted CEF traffic must reach the service.

Balanced service validation requires all eight three-reply destination flows, a three-reply reverse server probe and a complete actual HTTP200 service body. Minimum-only, nonfeasibility and failover exercises require delivered traffic in the changed state followed by fresh restored balanced traffic; config toggles alone cannot earn them.

Feasibility comparison retains FD10240 while R3 RD becomes10240 and total23040. Despite variance3 including the total metric threshold, strict feasibility excludes that path. Restoring R3 delay10 and R1 variance2 must restore the two weighted paths.

Per-attempt config/route epochs prevent stale traffic from earning a later stage. Six live and eight historical checks yield practice0/14, initial diagnosis1/14, baseline11/14 and full14/14. Completed reference supplies six live checks only. Earned observations persist through YAML export/import; fresh practice starts without history.
scope: Classic IOS IPv4 EIGRP internal multipath and CEF per-flow weighted forwarding. No new per-packet load-sharing command, hash bucket/hardware ASIC equivalence, exact sample packet ratio, physical bandwidth throughput model or fresh CML capture is claimed. The shared EIGRP installation fix also applies to existing named/IPv6 paths, with existing regression coverage; this lab teaches classic IPv4 only.
